change.title: pr-1-flat
change.description: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate a DateTimeField; the audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime"
findings.body: `get_item_key` (l.838-840) is copied from `Paginator`, which is for numeric keys. It runs `math.floor(getattr(item, "datetime"))`, and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). This raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` on a non-empty page. `value_from_cursor` (l.842-843) also returns the raw cursor value, where `DateTimePaginator` converts it back to a datetime. The `build_queryset` filter would therefore compare the datetime column with an integer. `GET .../audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true` by an eligible user returns a 500 whenever the org has audit log rows. It needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key handling, for example by subclassing it, if the paginator is kept at all.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to Django slicing, which asserts; the comments say the opposite
findings.body: The comments at l.874-880 say the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" and that this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing: `queryset[-5:96]` raises `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`. `Cursor.from_string` (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-61) accepts any integer offset from the `cursor` query parameter, for example `cursor=0:-5:0`. With `optimized_pagination=true` and an eligible user, a negative offset reaches `queryset[start_offset:stop]` (l.882) and returns a 500. Nothing is gained either. The branch has no valid behaviour to offer, and its comment about "permissions checked at the queryset level" justifies reading rows outside the page bounds. Remove the branch and clamp or reject negative offsets.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, which raises AttributeError
findings.body: `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). For any non-superuser without a membership in the org, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. The expression is evaluated for every request, before `use_optimized` is checked. That includes the default path that does not use the optimized paginator, so this change can turn requests that returned 200 into 500s. Evaluate it only when `use_optimized` is true, and guard against `member is None`. Also check how other endpoints test for superuser: `is_active_superuser(request)` is the usual check, and `request.user.is_superuser` alone does not show an active superuser session.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator behaviour changed with an incorrect rationale; the is_prev path still passes negative offsets
findings.body: This edit changes `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is used by every paginator that subclasses it. For a next-page cursor with a negative offset it now clamps to 0 instead of failing. The change is not needed for the new feature and its comment claims negative offsets are safe. For `is_prev` cursors the offset is still passed through unclamped, so `cursor=1:-5:1` still hits Django's negative-index assertion. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check at l.192 also keeps using the unclamped `offset`. Either validate offsets in `Cursor.from_string`, which fixes all paginators, or revert this hunk. Silently turning a malformed cursor into page 1 is a behaviour change for all callers.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result
findings.body: `get_result` (l.845-911) is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result`, and the only difference is the negative-offset branch. Any later fix to the base method will have to be applied twice. The docstring's claims ("optimized query path", "streamlined boundary condition handling") describe nothing in the code. No tests were added for the new paginator, the `optimized_pagination` flag or the clamping change, and tests for any of them would have exposed the first two problems above.

findings.title: Comment says negative offsets are allowed, but nothing changed
findings.body: The added comment says `Cursor` allows negative offsets for "efficient reverse pagination". `int(offset)` was already unchanged and no validation is added. The comment misleads readers into treating negative offsets as a supported feature, when downstream slicing rejects them.

contracts.action: Audit-log GET with optimized_pagination=true routes to OptimizedCursorPaginator
contracts.equivalent_path: Same endpoint's default branch using DateTimePaginator (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:230-241)
contracts.before_after: Before: always DateTimePaginator, which converts datetime to a ms timestamp key and back. After: the opt-in branch uses Paginator-style integer keys on a datetime column. The permission expression is also evaluated on every request.
contracts.visible_effect: The optimized request returns 500 on non-empty results (TypeError in math.floor(datetime)). Non-members hit AttributeError on every request.
contracts.failure_mode: Unhandled TypeError, AssertionError (negative slice) and AttributeError (member None) all surface as 500.

contracts.action: Negative cursor offset used in queryset slicing
contracts.before_after: Before: queryset[offset:stop] with an unclamped offset. After: the base clamps non-prev offsets, while the optimized paginator passes negative offsets straight through.
contracts.visible_effect: A crafted cursor such as 0:-5:0 gives a 500 instead of a validation error.
contracts.failure_mode: Django's negative-index assertion is unhandled, so there is a server error and no 4xx.

summary: The opt-in `optimized_pagination=true` path is broken. `OptimizedCursorPaginator` applies integer key math to the `datetime` column and raises `TypeError` on any non-empty page. Its negative-offset branch hits Django's "Negative indexing is not supported" assertion, so a crafted cursor gives a 500. The endpoint's new `organization_context.member.has_global_access` check raises `AttributeError` for non-superusers with no membership, and it runs on every request, including the default path. The `BasePaginator` clamp is an unrequested behaviour change on a shared class. The comments claiming negative offsets are safe are false. The change has no tests.
